biography.plain_text: Bill Gates is an American software entrepreneur who co-founded Microsoft with Paul Allen and later established the Gates Foundation with Melinda French Gates. His parents sent him to Lakeside School, where unusually early access to computing helped prepare him for the business. He left Harvard to develop software for the emerging personal-computer market.

long_biography.plain_text:
Bill Gates wrote Microsoft's first BASIC interpreter within the tight memory limits of the Altair computer. Paul Allen built a simulator so the team could test its work without owning the machine, while Monte Davidoff handled the mathematics routines. Gates concentrated on fitting the main program into four kilobytes, preserving room for customers' own programs.

The library programme he supported required practical revisions. The library foundation he created with Melinda supplied computers and training, but its first rollout in Alabama took longer than expected. Staff then consulted libraries earlier about installation and replaced dense manuals with shorter guides for users of different abilities.
